question.problem:
Let ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{40}$ be a random sample of size $n=40$ from a population with probability density function $$ f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}1, & 0\le x\le 1, \\ 0, & \text{otherwise}.\end{aligned} $$ Given that the population variance ${\sigma }^{2}=0.08,$ calculate $P(0.51<\overset{―}{X}<0.55).$ *Hint: Two tables of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ are given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,0.2\,$ $\,0.5793\,$ $\,0.5832\,$ $\,0.5871\,$
$\,0.3\,$ $\,0.6179\,$ $\,0.6217\,$ $\,0.6255\,$
$\,0.4\,$ $\,0.6554\,$ $\,0.6591\,$ $\,0.6628\,$
$z$$\,0.00\,$$\,0.01\,$$\,0.02\,$
$\,1.0\,$ $\,0.8413\,$ $\,0.8438\,$ $\,0.8461\,$
$\,1.1\,$ $\,0.8643\,$ $\,0.8665\,$ $\,0.8686\,$
$\,1.2\,$ $\,0.8849\,$ $\,0.8869\,$ $\,0.8888\,$
question.worked_solution:
Suppose that ${X}_{1},{X}_{2},…,{X}_{n}$ is a random sample of size $n$ from a population with population mean $\mu $ and population standard deviation $\sigma .$ The central limit theorem (or CLT) states that for sufficiently large $n,$ the distribution of the sample mean $\overset{―}{X}$ can be approximated as 

$$
\overset{―}{X}∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}).
$$

In our case:

- the sample size is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =40,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\mu  & =\text{E}[X] \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{\infty }x\,f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\cdot 1\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{1}{2} \\  & =0.5,\end{aligned}
$$

- the population variance is ${\sigma }^{2}=0.08.$

Therefore, by the CLT, we have that the distribution of the sample mean can be approximated as

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{X} & ∼N\,(\mu ,\frac{{\sigma }^{2}}{n}) \\  & ∼N\,(0.5,\frac{0.08}{40}) \\  & ∼N(0.5,0.002).\end{aligned}
$$

We want to find $P(0.51<\overset{―}{X}<0.55).$ So, we convert $\overset{―}{X}$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.51<\overset{―}{X}<0.55) & =P(\frac{0.51-0.5}{\sqrt{0.002}}<Z<\frac{0.55-0.5}{\sqrt{0.002}}) \\  & ≈P(0.22<Z<1.12) \\  & =P(Z<1.12)-P(Z<0.22) \\  & =Φ(1.12)-Φ(0.22)\end{aligned}
$$

From the tables, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(0.22)=0.5871, \\ Φ(1.12)=0.8686.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(0.51<\overset{―}{X}<0.55) & =Φ(1.12)-Φ(0.22) \\  & =0.8686-0.5871 \\  & =0.2815.\end{aligned}
$$
